answer: In an agent economy, participants must deposit a refundable stake that is slashed proportionally to detected duplicate registrations. This mechanism acts like a lantern that reveals true unique agents at the dawn of each new verification cycle. A would-be Sybil attacker trying to create many fake identities experiences a comet-like surge in required capital, because the bonding requirement compounds with every additional forged agent, quickly exhausting the attackers resources and rendering mass identity fraud unprofitable.
